Steamed Whole Fish for Lunar New Year

Served at: Lunar New Year (Chunjie)

Serves 4-6Prep 20 minCook 12-18 min

Serving a whole fish is a cornerstone of Lunar New Year celebrations, symbolizing abundance, prosperity, and a good beginning and end to the year. The word for 'fish' (yú) sounds like the word for 'surplus,' making it a potent symbol for having more than enough. This simple steaming method highlights the fish's natural sweetness and delicate texture.

Ingredients

  • 1 (1.5-2 lb / 680-900g) whole fish, such as red snapper, sea bass, or tilapia, scaled and gutted
  • 1 (2-inch / 5cm) piece fresh ginger, half sliced into thin rounds, half julienned
  • 4-5 scallions, white and light green parts cut into 2-inch (5cm) lengths, green parts thinly sliced for garnish
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) light soy sauce
  • 2 tablespoons (30ml) water or chicken broth
  • 1 teaspoon granulated sugar
  • 1 teaspoon sesame oil
  • 2 tablespoons (30ml) neutral oil (e.g., vegetable, canola)
  • Fresh cilantro sprigs, for garnish

Method

  1. Rinse the fish thoroughly under cold water, inside and out. Pat dry very well with paper towels.
  2. Make 2-3 diagonal slits on both sides of the fish, about 1/2 inch (1.25cm) deep, to help it cook evenly and absorb flavors.
  3. Place a few ginger slices and scallion lengths inside the fish cavity. Arrange the remaining ginger slices and scallion lengths on a heatproof plate that fits inside your steamer.
  4. Place the fish on top of the ginger and scallions on the plate.
  5. Bring water to a rolling boil in a wok or large pot fitted with a steamer rack. Carefully place the plate with the fish onto the steamer rack.
  6. Cover tightly and steam for 12-18 minutes, depending on the thickness of the fish. The fish is cooked when the flesh is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
  7. While the fish is steaming, prepare the sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, water or broth, sugar, and sesame oil until the sugar dissolves.
  8. Once the fish is cooked, carefully remove the plate from the steamer. Discard the cooked ginger and scallions from the plate and inside the fish cavity.
  9. Garnish the steamed fish generously with the julienned ginger, sliced green parts of scallions, and fresh cilantro sprigs.
  10. In a small saucepan, heat the neutral oil over medium-high heat until it just begins to smoke lightly.
  11. Carefully pour the hot oil directly over the fresh ginger, scallions, and cilantro on the fish. This will sizzle and release their aromas.
  12. Pour the prepared sauce evenly over the entire fish. Serve immediately with steamed white rice.

Tips

  • Choose the freshest fish possible; clear eyes, red gills, and firm flesh are good indicators.
  • Do not overcook the fish, as it will become dry. A good rule of thumb is 10 minutes per inch (2.5cm) of thickness at its thickest part.
  • For an extra touch of flavor, you can add a splash of Shaoxing wine to the steaming water or drizzle it over the fish before steaming.
